view: Macro went from a clear headwind to a mixed, easing headwind. Equity stress unwound sharply (VIX 35.9 -> 26.61, S5TH back above 50 at 53.08, equal-weight outperforming cap-weight over 1m), but the policy backdrop is unchanged and hawkish (CPI 3.7 vs Fed funds 4.0, Oct PPI 6.5, real 10y 2.77), and HY OAS widened to 3.76. Monday's +31.48% was mostly idiosyncratic (CEO reinstatement): market beta explains about 15% of it and the sector factor at most about 45%, so macro neither caused the rebound nor protects it.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 165.05 (Mon 2026-11-23 close; pre-market Tue run). next_2_weeks: up = close > 173.30, down = close < 156.80, range between, measured at the close on or before 2026-12-08 (Tue). this_quarter: to the 2026-12-31 close; next_quarter: to the 2027-03-31 close; up > 181.56, down < 148.55, range between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22 (n=259). Moved to 31/36/33: up -2, range -9, down +11. Range is cut because the volatility regime is still far above the sample norm (VIX 26.61; NVDA's last two sessions were -14.01% and +31.48%, and one-day moves of +15% or more happen on 0.32% of days). Down is raised because the down line (156.80) sits just under Monday's low 156.93, the 125.53-156.93 gap is open beneath, and core PCE (11-25), ISM (12-01/12-03) and NFP (12-04) all land inside the window with inflation still hot. FOMC (12-09) and CPI (12-10) fall just after the 2026-12-08 measurement close.

Base 39/43/18. Moved to 34/34/32 (up -5, range -9, down +14). The macro part: FOMC 2026-12-09, CPI 2026-12-10 (fcst 3.9 vs prev 3.7) and PPI 2026-12-15 all fall inside the window, and the Fed has no room to ease with CPI 3.7 against Fed funds 4.0. Part of the extra down weight is the SEC/accounting tail, which is outside my lane and which I count only once.

Base 50/31/19. Moved to 45/25/30 (up -5, range -6, down +11). The conditional rates point up (weekly RSI<=36, n=13: 69% up; 2w drop <=-15%, n=4: 100% up), but they are small, overlapping samples, and part of that rebound has already been paid out in one session. ISM 55.5 and a positive curve keep recession out of the base case, so up stays the largest bucket. A hawkish Fed plus widening credit keeps down above the base rate.
VIX 26.61 (-25.8% on the day) from 35.9 on 2026-11-20. The acute risk-off has eased but has not normalised: VIX is still above 25, so wide two-way swings remain likely.

S5TH 53.08 (+7.16), back above 50 from 45.92. Breadth has repaired above the line I set last run. RSP/SPY is now available: over 1m RSP is -1.97% and SPY -4.95% (ratio 0.2946). The selloff was concentrated in cap-weighted mega-caps rather than broad, which is good for the economy and less good for NVDA's factor specifically.

HY OAS 3.76 (chg +0.24), up from 3.52. Credit widened while equities bounced. The FRED series is at its latest release, so this print may reflect the 2026-11-20 selloff rather than Monday's rebound. It is now about halfway from 3.5 to my 4.0 contagion line. NFCI is unchanged at -0.48, still loose. This divergence is the main macro reason I do not follow the price up.

CPI YoY 3.7 vs Fed funds 4.0 (real policy rate about 0.3); Oct PPI YoY 6.5; CPI forecast for 2026-12-10 is 3.9. Claims IC4WSA 197,750 shows a tight labour market. fed_context: no new Fed decision. Nothing here has changed since 2026-11-22: no Fed put, and the risk of a hawkish surprise stays.
Real 10y 2.77 (chg -0.11), nominal 10y 4.934 (chg -0.008), 30y 5.304, TLT 81.69. The discount rate eased slightly but is still restrictive for long-duration equity. Rates did not drive Monday's move.
Curve positive (10y-3m 0.55, 10y-2y 0.29); ISM PMI 55.5 and new orders 55.5. Growth is expanding and there is no recession signal, which supports AI-capex demand. Inflation is the binding constraint.
DXY 104.33 (from 103.84) and USDJPY 159.34 (from 158.556). The dollar firmed during the rebound: a minor headwind, with no sign of yen-carry deleveraging.

Attribution of 2026-11-23: NVDA +31.48% vs SPX +4.73%, Nasdaq Comp +6.51%, SOX +14.03%, SMH +15.03%, AMD +6.85%, AVGO +3.0%. At beta 1, the market explains about 15% (about 4.7 of 31.5 pts) and Nasdaq about 21%. SOX explains about 45%, but NVDA is a large SOX/SMH weight, so that share is partly NVDA itself; ex-NVDA peers (AMD +6.85, AVGO +3.0) suggest the true sector share is closer to 20-25%. The residual is roughly 17-25 pts and is idiosyncratic (reinstatement). Beta is not in the slice. Over 5 sessions NVDA is +3.8% vs SOX -1.0% and SPX -3.68%; 1m NVDA -21.77% vs SOX -10.19%. NVDA's underperformance since October remains mostly stock-specific.

Inside the 2w window (to 2026-12-08): 11-25 GDP Q3 2nd est, core PCE, income/spending, durables; 11-26 closed; 11-27 half-day (thin liquidity); 12-01 ISM manufacturing (prev 55.5) and a Huang House interview whose status is unconfirmed after reinstatement; 12-02 NVDA ex-dividend; 12-03 ISM services and a requested Senate Banking hearing; 12-04 NFP and the approximate 10-Q deadline. Inside the quarter: 12-09 FOMC, 12-10 CPI (fcst 3.9, prev 3.7), 12-15 PPI. A retail sales date is not in the slice.

what_would_change_my_mind: More bullish (2w): core PCE on 2026-11-25 at or below expectations, VIX closing below 22 by 2026-12-08, and HY OAS back below 3.5 with S5TH holding above 50.
More bullish (quarters): FOMC 2026-12-09 holds without a hiking bias and CPI 2026-12-10 prints at or below 3.7 (vs 3.9 fcst), with real 10y below 2.7.
More bearish: HY OAS above 4.0 with NFCI rising above -0.30 before 2026-12-31 (equity risk-off becoming a credit event).

More bearish: VIX closes back above 30 before 2026-12-08 while NVDA closes below 156.80 (reach check: -5% by 2026-12-08 = 41.6% of past windows, reachable), meaning the rebound has failed in a renewed risk-off.
More bearish (quarters): FOMC 2026-12-09 hikes or signals several hikes and CPI 2026-12-10 is at or above 3.9, with 30y back above 5.5.
More bearish: ISM manufacturing on 2026-12-01 below 52 or a negative NFP on 2026-12-04 (stagflation mix with no Fed relief).
Expected line (not a trigger): PCE 11-25, Thanksgiving half-day 11-27, ISM 12-01/12-03, NFP 12-04, FOMC 12-09 and CPI 12-10 will all happen; only their outcomes, phrased above, move my view.
notes_for_chair: Signs before 2026-11-23 (inputs/readings_2026-11-22.json) that pointed to a sharp rebound: (1) VIX 35.9 after a +26.28% day and a Nasdaq week that was the worst since March 2020: capitulation-grade fear that usually mean-reverts. (2) Equity stress without credit stress: HY OAS only 3.52 (+0.05) and NFCI -0.48 (loose), so the selloff was a de-rating, not a funding crisis. (3) No recession signal: ISM 55.5 and a positive curve (10y-3m 0.6). (4) Flight to safety had eased the discount rate (10y -0.10 to 4.95). (5) S5TH at 45.92 was only modestly below 50, which leaves room for a fast repair (it went to 53.08). (6) The conditional base rate for a 2w drop <=-15% (n=4) was 50/50/0 with no down outcomes, though the sample is tiny.

Signs that did NOT point to a rebound: (1) Hawkish Fed with no put: CPI 3.7 vs Fed funds 4.0, PPI 6.5, Musalem wanting several hikes. (2) Restrictive real 10y 2.88 and 30y 5.337. (3) Credit direction was widening (and the latest print, 3.76, is wider still). (4) Breadth had broken below 50 and the dollar/yen were firm. (5) Most importantly, nothing in macro could forecast a +31.48% day: one-day moves of +15% or more occur on 0.32% of NVDA days, and the catalyst (Huang reinstated, the reversal of the TB2 premise) was idiosyncratic. Macro readings at most set up a better-than-usual chance of a relief rally. My 2026-11-22 macro 2w call (35/29/36 at 125.53) gave up and down nearly equal tails; up has now been hit with a lot of room to spare. Lesson for the log: at capitulation-grade VIX with credit calm, macro should tilt toward up rather than hold symmetric tails. Whether this rebound is a single-day relief or a regime change is not yet settled by macro data.

Update vs 2026-11-22 (35/29/36, 34/32/34, 42/24/34 at 125.53): re-based to 165.05. Range is lifted on 2w because VIX has fallen 26%, the quarter buckets are roughly balanced, and next-quarter up is lifted 3 points because breadth repaired. Confidence goes from 30 to 27, because macro explains much less of this move than of last week's.

Before vs after the print: the 2026-11-17 beat was followed by a macro and sector risk-off that magnified stock-specific news. After reinstatement, the driver is again mostly stock-specific. Macro is a moderate headwind (hawkish Fed, wider HY) set against an improved risk appetite (VIX, breadth).

Measurement-day note: the 2w close (2026-12-08) comes the day before the FOMC and two days before CPI, so pre-event positioning may compress moves on that day. NFP on 2026-12-04 is ambiguous in this regime (good for growth, bad for hike odds).

Cross-domain: TB2's premise (CEO departure) has reversed; whether TB2 is lifted is the chair's ruling. The SEC/accounting story, the 10-Q status (deadline about 2026-12-04) and whether the congressional interviews still happen are outside my lane, but they cluster in the same 12-01..12-04 week as ISM and NFP. Macro gives no evidence for TB4 (ISM 55.5).

Ladder pacing (macro view, proposal only; owner approval required; no order to be placed or executed): catalysts still cluster around 11-25 and 12-01..12-10. With VIX at 26.61 and the gap open down to 125.53, any tranche spacing should still be checked against the elevated ATR. Spreading across time, before and after FOMC/CPI, remains my macro suggestion.

Pre-mortem: if this is badly wrong in three months, the likely reason is either (a) the reinstatement plus repaired breadth started a V-recovery toward the 179.92-185.22 gap and beyond while the Fed simply held, which would make my down weights recency bias; or (b) HY OAS crossed 4.0 and a hawkish FOMC/CPI turned this into a credit-led drawdown that refilled the 125.53-156.93 gap, which would make 32-33% down too low.
